query: What recurring issues drive resolution inefficiency?

per_column.name: hardware_device_category
per_column.rationale: The type of device involved is a contextual attribute of the incident, not an aspect of WHY resolution was inefficient. It may correlate with inefficiency but is not itself a reason for it.

per_column.name: incident_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the nature of the incident, not the constitutive reasons for inefficiency. A functionality_failure is not an inefficiency reason; it is a descriptor of the problem being resolved.

per_column.name: resource_assignment_pattern
per_column.rationale: Transfers between resolvers (single_resolver vs transferred) is a genuine aspect OF resolution inefficiency -- routing/ownership churn is a constitutive contributor to inefficient resolution.

per_column.name: description_specificity_level
per_column.rationale: Poor or generic problem descriptions are a constitutive facet of inefficiency: inadequate information at intake directly hampers resolution. This is an aspect of the reasons, not an external attribute.

per_column.name: issue_scope_impact
per_column.rationale: The scope/impact of the issue characterizes severity of the incident, not a reason resolution was inefficient. It is a driver/correlate rather than a part of the inefficiency itself.

per_column.name: resolution_path_hint
per_column.rationale: The likely resolution route describes the remedy needed, not a reason for inefficiency. It is a property of the fix rather than a constitutive aspect of why resolution was inefficient.

per_column.name: caller_persistence
per_column.rationale: Repeat reporting reflects unresolved/recurring interaction overhead, a plausible aspect of inefficiency, though it partially overlaps with chronic/reopened issues.

per_column.name: reopened_or_chronic_issue
per_column.rationale: Reopened/chronic incidents are a direct constitutive facet of resolution inefficiency: rework and failure-to-resolve-first-time are core inefficiency aspects. Overlaps somewhat with caller_persistence.

judge.rationale: Half the added columns are contextual descriptors of the incident (device, type, scope, resolution path) that predict or characterize incidents rather than decompose the reasons for inefficiency; these fail the meronymy test. Only four columns (assignment churn, description quality, caller persistence, reopened/chronic) are genuine facets of inefficiency. Among these, caller_persistence and reopened_or_chronic_issue overlap substantially (both capture recurrence/unresolved-issue signal), lowering mutual exclusivity. As a facet set they also miss key constitutive aspects of resolution inefficiency such as SLA/time delays, wait/idle states, knowledge/skill gaps, and priority-handling mismatches, so exhaustiveness is limited.
